#### References to other Issues or PRs


#### Brief description of what is fixed or changed

Mod has precedence like Mul so it printed with parentheses surrounding it when it appeared as a factor in an expression. This is not necessary since it is not shown in inline form. The printing need for parentheses is now handled in the printers while leaving the global precedence unchanged.

#### Other comments


#### AI Generation Disclosure

Collaborative effort with ChatGPT after identifying the issue while working on other Mod related issues.

#### Release Notes


<!-- BEGIN RELEASE NOTES -->
NO ENTRY

@@ -54,6 +54,7 @@ class CodePrinter(StrPrinter):
     """
     The base class for code-printing subclasses.
     """
+    _mod_precedence = PRECEDENCE["Mul"]
 
     _operators = {
         'and': '&&',
diff --git a/sympy/printing/str.py b/sympy/printing/str.py
index 56f5247a748b..c602f5461f01 100644
--- a/sympy/printing/str.py
+++ b/sympy/printing/str.py
@@ -7,6 +7,7 @@
 
 from sympy.core import S, Rational, Pow, Basic, Mul, Number, UnevaluatedExpr
 from sympy.core.function import Lambda
+from sympy.core.mod import Mod
 from sympy.core.mul import _keep_coeff
 from sympy.core.numbers import Integer
 from sympy.core.relational import Relational
@@ -24,6 +25,9 @@
 
 class StrPrinter(Printer):
     printmethod = "_sympystr"
+
+    _mod_precedence = PRECEDENCE["Func"]
+
     _default_settings: dict[str, Any] = {
         "order": None,
         "full_prec": "auto",
@@ -38,7 +42,8 @@ class StrPrinter(Printer):
     _relationals: dict[str, str] = {}
 
     def parenthesize(self, item, level, strict=False):
-        if (precedence(item) < level) or ((not strict) and precedence(item) <= level):
+        prec = self._mod_precedence if isinstance(item, Mod) else precedence(item)
+        if prec < level or (not strict and prec <= level):
             return "(%s)" % self._print(item)
         else:
             return self._print(item)

@@ -1360,3 +1361,15 @@ def test_printing_stats():
 def test_issue_30343():
     f = Function('f')
     assert str(f(nan) + f(1)) == "f(nan) + f(1)"
+
+
+def test_Mod():
+    m = Mod(x, y, evaluate=False)
+    assert str(3*m) == "3*Mod(x, y)"
+    assert str(m*sin(x)) == "sin(x)*Mod(x, y)"
+    assert str(m**2) == "Mod(x, y)**2"
+    assert str(1/m) == "1/Mod(x, y)"
+    assert str(m*Mod(x + 1, y, evaluate=False)) == \
+        "Mod(x, y)*Mod(x + 1, y)"
+    assert str(Mod(12**(x + 1), 21)) == \
+        "3*Mod(12**(x + 1)/3, 7)"
